$comment: Maps a country's Wikidata P122 (basic form of government) onto the leader-resolution class that decides which portrait leads the dossier header. Matching is LABEL-driven, not Q-id driven, and deliberately so: Q-ids for forms of government could not be confirmed from this build environment, and a wrong Q-id would silently misclassify a country's entire header. An English label from the Wikidata label service is checkable by eye; a wrong Q-id is not. The qids array on each rule is empty pending verification when egress opens — populate it then and label matching becomes the fallback rather than the primary.
matching: Rules are evaluated in array order and the first whose `contains` all appear in the lowercased label wins. Order matters: 'semi-presidential' must be tested before 'presidential', and both monarchy specialisations before bare 'monarchy'.
unmatchedBehaviour: A label matching no rule yields the 'undetermined' class. The resolver then shows whichever of head of state / head of government exists, states plainly that the form of government could not be determined, and tags the resolution DERIVED. It never guesses a class.

rules.note: Military junta. Leader shown with the literal title in use, never smoothed to 'President'.
Monarch holds real executive power and leads the header.
Head of government leads; the monarch appears as a smaller secondary portrait.
Head of government leads; the ceremonial president appears as a smaller secondary portrait.
The president holds executive power, so leads the header even though a prime minister also exists.
Bare 'monarchy' with no qualifier. Tested last so the constitutional and absolute cases match first.
